        })
    }

    /// Create a telemetry emitter from a `TelemetryConfig`.
    ///
    /// Selects the right constructor based on configured sinks:
    /// - OTLP enabled       → creates OTLP sink with async shutdown
    /// - Hooks configured   → [`with_hooks`](Self::with_hooks)
    /// - Stdout enabled     → [`with_stdout`](Self::with_stdout)
    /// - Otherwise          → [`new`](Self::new) (file sink only)
    pub fn from_config(worker_id: WorkerId, config: &TelemetryConfig) -> Result<Self> {
        Self::from_config_with_identity(worker_id, config, &TelemetryIdentity::default())
    }

    /// Create a telemetry emitter from configuration with worker identity metadata.
    ///
    /// This is the construction path used by a running worker. Keeping the
    /// identity separate from `TelemetryConfig` avoids putting runtime-resolved
    /// adapter details into persisted configuration while ensuring every OTLP
    /// signal receives the same worker metadata.
    pub fn from_config_with_identity(
        worker_id: WorkerId,
        config: &TelemetryConfig,
        identity: &TelemetryIdentity,
    ) -> Result<Self> {
        let session_id = generate_session_id();
        let (sender, receiver) = mpsc::unbounded_channel();

        let mut sinks: Vec<Box<dyn Sink>> = Vec::new();
        let mut otlp_shutdown = None;
        let mut file_sink: Option<Arc<FileSink>> = None;

        // File sink is created only if enabled in config
        // When disabled, telemetry falls back to stdout/hook sinks only
        if config.file_sink.enabled {
            // Use configured log_dir if set, otherwise use default
            let file_sink_result = if let Some(ref log_dir) = config.file_sink.log_dir {
                FileSink::with_dir(log_dir.clone(), &worker_id, &session_id)
            } else {
                FileSink::new(&worker_id, &session_id)
            };

            match file_sink_result {
                Ok(s) => {
                    // Write boot event directly to file BEFORE spawning writer thread.
                    // Uses a 5-second timeout to prevent indefinite blocking on hung filesystems.
                    let version = env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION");
                    if let Err(e) = s.write_boot_event_direct(&worker_id, &session_id, version) {
                        // Check if this is a timeout error (filesystem may be hung)
                        let error_msg = e.to_string();
                        if error_msg.contains("timed out")
                            || error_msg.contains("filesystem may be hung")
                        {
                            eprintln!(
                                "NEEDLE WARNING: boot event write timed out after 5s - filesystem may be hung or very slow"
                            );
                            eprintln!("  Continuing without boot event in log file. Worker will still function.");
                            eprintln!(
                                "  Check: disk space, NFS mounts, filesystem latency, I/O errors"
                            );
                        }
                        tracing::warn!(error = %e, "failed to write boot event directly to file");
                    }
                    file_sink = Some(Arc::new(s));
                    // Arc<FileSink> implements Sink via the blanket impl
                    if let Some(ref fs) = file_sink {
                        sinks.push(Box::new(Arc::clone(fs)));
                    }
                }
                Err(e) => tracing::warn!(error = %e, "failed to create telemetry file sink"),
            }
        }

        // OTLP sink (feature-gated)
        #[cfg(feature = "otlp")]
        {
            if config.otlp_sink.enabled {
                // Convert Arc<FileSink> to Option<Box<dyn Sink>> for OtlpSink
                let file_sink_for_otlp = file_sink
                    .as_ref()
                    .map(|fs| Box::new(Arc::clone(fs)) as Box<dyn Sink>);

                match OtlpSink::new(
                    worker_id.clone(),
                    session_id.clone(),
                    &config.otlp_sink,
                    file_sink_for_otlp,
                    identity.agent.as_deref(),
                    identity.model.as_deref(),
                    identity.workspace.as_deref().and_then(Path::to_str),
                ) {
                    Ok(otlp) => {
                        let otlp_arc = Arc::new(otlp);
                        sinks.push(Box::new(Arc::clone(&otlp_arc)));
                        otlp_shutdown = Some(OtlpShutdown::Sink(otlp_arc));
                        tracing::info!("OTLP sink initialized: {}", config.otlp_sink.endpoint);
                    }
                    Err(e) => {
                        tracing::warn!(error = %e, "failed to create OTLP sink, continuing without it");
                    }
                }
            }
        }

        // Stdout sink
        if config.stdout_sink.enabled {
            sinks.push(Box::new(StdoutSink::new(&config.stdout_sink)));
        }

        // Hook sinks
        if !config.hooks.is_empty() {
            sinks.push(Box::new(HookSink::new(&config.hooks)?));
        }

        let sequence = Arc::new(AtomicU64::new(0));
        let pending = PendingWriter { receiver, sinks };

        Ok(Telemetry {
            worker_id,
            session_id,
            sequence,
            sender: Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(Some(sender))),
            pending_writer: Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(Some(pending))),
            writer_handle: Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(None)),
            otlp_shutdown: Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(otlp_shutdown)),
        })
    }

    /// Create a telemetry emitter backed by a real `FileSink` in a custom
    /// directory (for testing the `start()`/`shutdown()` lifecycle).
    ///
    /// Returns `(Telemetry, log_file_path)`. Call `start()` from inside a
    /// tokio runtime, emit events, then `shutdown().await` — the BufWriter
    /// will be flushed before `shutdown()` returns.
    #[cfg(test)]
    pub fn with_log_dir_and_path(
        worker_id: WorkerId,
        log_dir: &std::path::Path,
    ) -> Result<(Self, std::path::PathBuf)> {
        // Fixed session ID so the caller knows the exact file path.
        let session_id = "testbeef".to_string();
        let (sender, receiver) = mpsc::unbounded_channel();
        let file_sink = FileSink::with_dir(log_dir.to_path_buf(), &worker_id, &session_id)?;
        let path = file_sink.path().to_path_buf();
        // Write boot event directly to file (for consistency with production code).
        let version = env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION");
        let _ = file_sink.write_boot_event_direct(&worker_id, &session_id, version);
        let sequence = Arc::new(AtomicU64::new(0));
        let sinks: Vec<Box<dyn Sink>> = vec![Box::new(file_sink)];
        let pending = PendingWriter { receiver, sinks };
        Ok((
            Telemetry {
                worker_id,
                session_id,
                sequence,
                sender: Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(Some(sender))),
                pending_writer: Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(Some(pending))),
                writer_handle: Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(None)),
                otlp_shutdown: Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(None)),
            },
            path,
        ))
    }

    /// Create a telemetry emitter with a custom sink (for testing).
    #[cfg(any(test, feature = "integration"))]
    pub fn with_sink(worker_id: WorkerId, sink: impl Sink + 'static) -> Self {
        let session_id = "test0000".to_string();
        let (sender, receiver) = mpsc::unbounded_channel::<WriterMessage>();
        let sequence = Arc::new(AtomicU64::new(0));

        tokio::spawn(async move {
            let mut rx = receiver;
            while let Some(msg) = rx.recv().await {
                if let WriterMessage::Event(event) = msg {
                    if let Err(e) = sink.accept(&event) {
                        tracing::warn!(error = %e, "test sink accept failed");
                    }
                }
            }
        });

        Telemetry {
            worker_id,
            session_id,
            sequence,
            sender: Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(Some(sender))),
            pending_writer: Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(None)),
            writer_handle: Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(None)),
            otlp_shutdown: Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(None)),
        }
    }

    /// Emit an event. Non-blocking — returns immediately.
    ///
    /// Returns `Err` only if the channel is disconnected (background task died).
    pub fn emit(&self, kind: EventKind) -> Result<()> {
        let seq = self.sequence.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
        let (trace_id, span_id) = current_trace_ids();
        let event = TelemetryEvent {
            timestamp: Utc::now(),
            event_type: kind.event_type().to_string(),
            worker_id: self.worker_id.clone(),
            session_id: self.session_id.clone(),
            sequence: seq,
            bead_id: kind.bead_id(),
            workspace: None,
            duration_ms: kind.duration_ms(),
            data: kind.to_data(),
            trace_id,
            span_id,
        };
        tracing::debug!(event_type = %event.event_type, seq, "telemetry event");
        // Use try_lock() to avoid blocking indefinitely if the telemetry writer
        // is stuck holding the lock. If the lock is contended, we log and return
        // Ok(()) to allow the worker to continue.
        match self.sender.try_lock() {
            Ok(guard) => {
                if let Some(ref s) = *guard {
                    s.send(WriterMessage::Event(event)).ok(); // ok() — never block, never panic
                }
                Ok(())
            }
            Err(_) => {
                tracing::warn!(
                    event_type = %event.event_type,
                    seq,
                    "telemetry sender lock contended, skipping emit"
                );
                Ok(())
            }
        }
    }

    /// Emit an event without blocking — uses try_lock() instead of lock().
    ///
    /// Returns `Ok(())` if emitted successfully or if the lock is contended
    /// (gracefully degrades). Returns `Err` only if the channel is disconnected.
    ///
    /// Use this in timeout recovery paths where blocking on emit() would
    /// prevent the worker from recovering.
    pub fn emit_try_lock(&self, kind: EventKind) -> Result<()> {
        let seq = self.sequence.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
        let (trace_id, span_id) = current_trace_ids();
        let event = TelemetryEvent {
            timestamp: Utc::now(),
            event_type: kind.event_type().to_string(),
            worker_id: self.worker_id.clone(),
            session_id: self.session_id.clone(),
            sequence: seq,
            bead_id: kind.bead_id(),
            workspace: None,
            duration_ms: kind.duration_ms(),
            data: kind.to_data(),
            trace_id,
            span_id,
        };
        // Use try_lock() to avoid blocking indefinitely if the telemetry writer
        // is stuck holding the lock. If the lock is contended, we log and return
        // Ok(()) to allow the worker to continue.
        match self.sender.try_lock() {
            Ok(guard) => {
                if let Some(ref s) = *guard {
                    s.send(WriterMessage::Event(event)).ok();
                }
                Ok(())
            }
            Err(_) => {
                tracing::warn!(
                    event_type = %event.event_type,
                    seq,
                    "telemetry sender lock contended, skipping emit in timeout recovery path"
                );
                Ok(())
            }
        }
    }

    /// Force-flush all buffered events to disk (synchronous).
    ///
    /// Sends a flush request through the writer channel and waits (up to
    /// `timeout`) for the writer task to flush its BufWriter. Used after
    /// `worker.booting` so the event is visible on disk even if subsequent
    /// init steps block.
    ///
    /// NOTE: This uses `blocking_recv()` and must be called from outside a
    /// tokio runtime (e.g., in `run_worker` before `rt.block_on`). Use
    /// `force_flush_async()` from within async contexts.
    pub fn force_flush(&self, timeout: std::time::Duration) -> Result<()> {
        let (tx, rx) = tokio::sync::oneshot::channel();
        // Use try_lock() to avoid blocking indefinitely if the telemetry writer
        // is stuck holding the lock.
        match self.sender.try_lock() {
            Ok(guard) => {
                if let Some(ref s) = *guard {
                    s.send(WriterMessage::Flush(tx)).ok();
                }
            }
            Err(_) => {
                tracing::warn!("telemetry sender lock contended in force_flush, skipping flush");
                return Ok(()); // Don't fail — the writer will eventually flush
            }
        }
        // Block until the writer task flushes or timeout.
        // Spawn a thread to handle the blocking recv with a timeout.
        let handle = std::thread::spawn(move || rx.blocking_recv());
        let start = std::time::Instant::now();
        loop {
            if handle.is_finished() {
                return Ok(());
            }
            if start.elapsed() >= timeout {
                tracing::warn!("force_flush timed out after {:?}", timeout);
                return Ok(()); // Don't fail — the writer will eventually flush
            }
            std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(50));
        }
    }

    /// Force-flush all buffered events to disk (async).
    ///
    /// Async version of `force_flush()` that can be called from within a
    /// tokio runtime. Use this in `Worker::run()` and other async contexts.
    pub async fn force_flush_async(&self, timeout: std::time::Duration) -> Result<()> {
        let (tx, rx) = tokio::sync::oneshot::channel();
        // Use try_lock() to avoid blocking indefinitely if the telemetry writer
        // is stuck holding the lock.
        match self.sender.try_lock() {
            Ok(guard) => {
                if let Some(ref s) = *guard {
                    s.send(WriterMessage::Flush(tx)).ok();
                }
            }
            Err(_) => {
                tracing::warn!(
                    "telemetry sender lock contended in force_flush_async, skipping flush"
                );
                return Ok(()); // Don't fail — the writer will eventually flush
            }
        }
        // Wait for the writer task to flush, with timeout.
        match tokio::time::timeout(timeout, rx).await {
            Ok(Ok(())) => Ok(()),
            Ok(Err(_)) => Ok(()), // Channel closed, writer already flushed
            Err(_) => {
                tracing::warn!("force_flush_async timed out after {:?}", timeout);
                Ok(())
            }
        }
    }

    /// Emit an event synchronously, writing directly to the file sink.
    ///
    /// This bypasses the async channel and writes immediately to the file.
    /// Use this for critical early-boot events (like `worker.booting`) that
    /// must be visible even if the async writer hasn't started yet.
    ///
    /// Returns `Err` if the pending writer is not available (already started)
    /// or if writing to the file fails.
    pub fn emit_sync(&self, kind: EventKind) -> Result<()> {
        let seq = self.sequence.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
        let (trace_id, span_id) = current_trace_ids();
        let event = TelemetryEvent {
            timestamp: Utc::now(),
            event_type: kind.event_type().to_string(),
            worker_id: self.worker_id.clone(),
            session_id: self.session_id.clone(),
            sequence: seq,
            bead_id: kind.bead_id(),
            workspace: None,
            duration_ms: kind.duration_ms(),
            data: kind.to_data(),
            trace_id,
            span_id,
        };

        // Take the pending writer temporarily to write directly to sinks.
        let pending_guard = self.pending_writer.lock().unwrap();
        if let Some(ref pending) = *pending_guard {
            // Write directly to each sink (typically just FileSink).
            for sink in &pending.sinks {
                if let Err(e) = sink.accept(&event) {
                    tracing::warn!(error = %e, "sync emit to sink failed");
                }
            }
            Ok(())
        } else {
            // Pending writer already consumed by start().
            Err(anyhow::anyhow!("cannot emit_sync after start()"))
        }
    }

    /// Return a reference to the session ID for log path discovery.
    pub fn session_id(&self) -> &str {
        &self.session_id
    }

    /// Return a reference to the worker ID.
    pub fn worker_id(&self) -> &str {
        &self.worker_id
    }

    /// Create a telemetry emitter writing to a specific log directory.
    ///
    /// Use this when the config specifies a custom log path. Does not spawn
    /// any async tasks. Call [`start()`](Self::start) from within a tokio
    /// runtime context before emitting events.
    pub fn with_log_dir(worker_id: WorkerId, log_dir: &Path) -> Self {
        let session_id = generate_session_id();
        let (sender, receiver) = mpsc::unbounded_channel();

        let mut sinks: Vec<Box<dyn Sink>> = Vec::new();
        match FileSink::with_dir(log_dir.to_path_buf(), &worker_id, &session_id) {
            Ok(s) => sinks.push(Box::new(s)),
            Err(e) => tracing::warn!(error = %e, "failed to create telemetry file sink"),
        }

        let sequence = Arc::new(AtomicU64::new(0));
        let pending = PendingWriter { receiver, sinks };

        Telemetry {
            worker_id,
            session_id,
            sequence,
            sender: Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(Some(sender))),
            pending_writer: Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(Some(pending))),
            writer_handle: Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(None)),
            otlp_shutdown: Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(None)),
        }
    }

    /// Start the background writer task.
    ///
    /// Must be called from within a tokio runtime context (e.g. inside
    /// `block_on` or an async function). Calling this more than once on
    /// the same handle is a no-op.
    pub fn start(&self) {
        let pending = self.pending_writer.lock().unwrap().take();
        if let Some(pw) = pending {
            let handle = Self::spawn_writer(pw.receiver, pw.sinks, None);
            *self.writer_handle.lock().unwrap() = Some(handle);
        }
    }

    /// Start the background writer task and wait for it to be ready.
    ///

   201	
   202	            // Compute workspace lock path
   203	            let lock_path = workspace_lock_path(&self.lock_dir, &candidate.workspace);
   204	
   205	            // Acquire flock with timeout
   206	            let lock_file = match acquire_flock(&lock_path).await {
   207	                Ok(f) => f,
   208	                Err(e) => {
   209	                    tracing::warn!(bead_id = %bead_id, error = %e, "flock timeout, skipping");
   210	                    self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::ClaimFailed {
   211	                        bead_id: bead_id.clone(),
   212	                        reason: format!("flock timeout: {e}"),
   213	                    })?;
   214	                    // Set Error status on the bead.claim span
   215	                    tracing::Span::current().record("otel.status_code", 2u64);
   216	                    tracing::Span::current()
   217	                        .record("otel.status_description", format!("flock timeout: {e}"));
   218	                    return Ok(ClaimOutcome::StoreError(e));
   219	                }
   220	            };
   221	
   222	            // Verify bead is still claimable (status=open, no assignee)
   223	            let (current, claim_event_count) =
   224	                match self.store.show_with_claim_history(bead_id).await {
   225	                    Ok(b) => b,
   226	                    Err(e) => {
   227	                        drop(lock_file);
   228	                        self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::ClaimFailed {
   229	                            bead_id: bead_id.clone(),
   230	                            reason: format!("verify failed: {e}"),
   231	                        })?;
   232	                        // Set Error status on the bead.claim span
   233	                        tracing::Span::current().record("otel.status_code", 2u64);
   234	                        tracing::Span::current()
   235	                            .record("otel.status_description", format!("verify failed: {e}"));
   236	                        return Ok(ClaimOutcome::StoreError(e));
   237	                    }
   238	                };
   239	
   240	            if current.status != BeadStatus::Open || current.assignee.is_some() {
   241	                drop(lock_file);
   242	                // Distinguish stale-assignee from race-lost: race_lost means another worker
   243	                // won the race (status changed), not that this bead has a leftover assignee.
   244	                if current.status == BeadStatus::Open && current.assignee.is_some() {
   245	                    self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::ClaimFailed {
   246	                        bead_id: bead_id.clone(),
   247	                        reason: "stale assignee".to_string(),
   248	                    })?;
   249	                } else {
   250	                    self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::ClaimRaceLost {
   251	                        bead_id: bead_id.clone(),
   252	                    })?;
   253	                }
   254	                // Apply backoff before trying next candidate (same as store.claim RaceLost path)
   255	                if attempts < self.max_retries {
   256	                    tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(
   257	                        self.retry_backoff_ms * u64::from(attempts),
   258	                    ))
   259	                    .await;
   260	                }
   261	                continue;
   262	            }
   263	
   264	            let in_memory_limit = if claim_event_count.is_none() {
   265	                self.check_event_limit(bead_id)
   266	            } else {
   267	                None
   268	            };
   269	            if let Some(event_count) = claim_event_count.or(in_memory_limit) {
   270	                if event_count >= MAX_CLAIM_EVENTS_PER_BEAD {
   271	                    drop(lock_file);
   272	                    let reason = self.trip_event_limit(bead_id, event_count).await?;
   273	                    return Ok(ClaimOutcome::Suspect {
   274	                        bead_id: bead_id.clone(),
   275	                        consecutive_errors: event_count,
   276	                        last_error: reason,
   277	                    });
   278	                }
   279	            }
   280	
   281	            // Attempt claim via store
   282	            let result = self.store.claim(bead_id, actor).await;
   283	            drop(lock_file);
   284	
   285	            match result {
   286	                Ok(ClaimResult::Claimed(bead)) => {
   287	                    tracing::Span::current().record("needle.claim.result", "succeeded");
   288	                    // Clear error counter on successful claim
   289	                    self.clear_claim_errors(bead_id);
   290	                    self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::ClaimSuccess {
   291	                        bead_id: bead_id.clone(),
   292	                        priority: candidate.priority as i32,
   293	                        strand: strand.to_string(),
   294	                    })?;
   295	                    return Ok(ClaimOutcome::Claimed(bead));
   296	                }
   297	                Ok(ClaimResult::RaceLost { .. }) => {
   298	                    tracing::Span::current().record("needle.claim.result", "race_lost");
   299	                    self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::ClaimRaceLost {
   300	                        bead_id: bead_id.clone(),
   301	                    })?;
   302	                    if attempts < self.max_retries {
   303	                        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(
   304	                            self.retry_backoff_ms * u64::from(attempts),
   305	                        ))
   306	                        .await;
   307	                    }
   308	                    continue;
   309	                }
   310	                Ok(ClaimResult::NotClaimable { reason }) => {
   311	                    tracing::Span::current().record("needle.claim.result", &reason);
   312	                    self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::ClaimFailed {
   313	                        bead_id: bead_id.clone(),
   314	                        reason: reason.clone(),
   315	                    })?;
   316	                    continue;
   317	                }
   318	                Ok(ClaimResult::ClaimError { reason }) => {
   319	                    tracing::Span::current().record("needle.claim.result", &reason);
   320	                    self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::ClaimFailed {
   321	                        bead_id: bead_id.clone(),
   322	                        reason: reason.clone(),
   323	                    })?;
   324	                    // Record claim error and check if threshold reached
   325	                    if let Some((consecutive, last_error)) =
   326	                        self.record_claim_error(bead_id, &reason)
   327	                    {
   328	                        self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::ClaimErrorThreshold {
   329	                            bead_id: bead_id.clone(),
   330	                            consecutive_errors: consecutive,
   331	                            last_error: last_error.clone(),
   332	                        })?;
   333	                        // Set Error status on the bead.claim span
   334	                        tracing::Span::current().record("otel.status_code", 2u64);
   335	                        tracing::Span::current().record("otel.status_description", &last_error);
   336	                        return Ok(ClaimOutcome::Suspect {
   337	                            bead_id: bead_id.clone(),
   338	                            consecutive_errors: consecutive,
   339	                            last_error,
   340	                        });
   341	                    }
   342	                    // Continue to next candidate when threshold not yet reached
   343	                    continue;
   344	                }
   345	                Ok(ClaimResult::Suspect {
   346	                    bead_id: id,
   347	                    consecutive_errors,
   348	                    last_error,
   349	                }) => {
   350	                    // Bead is already marked suspect — propagate Suspect immediately
   351	                    tracing::warn!(
   352	                        bead_id = %id,
   353	                        consecutive_errors,
   354	                        %last_error,
   355	                        "bead already marked suspect, propagating without retry"
   356	                    );
   357	                    // Set Error status on the bead.claim span
   358	                    tracing::Span::current().record("otel.status_code", 2u64);
   359	                    tracing::Span::current().record(
   360	                        "otel.status_description",
   361	                        format!(
   362	                            "suspect: {} consecutive errors: {}",
   363	                            consecutive_errors, last_error
   364	                        ),
   365	                    );
   366	                    return Ok(ClaimOutcome::Suspect {
   367	                        bead_id: id,
   368	                        consecutive_errors,
   369	                        last_error,
   370	                    });
   371	                }
   372	                Err(e) => {
   373	                    let reason = format!("store error: {e}");
   374	                    tracing::Span::current().record("needle.claim.result", &reason);
   375	                    self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::ClaimFailed {
   376	                        bead_id: bead_id.clone(),
   377	                        reason: reason.clone(),
   378	                    })?;
   379	                    // Record claim error and check if threshold reached
   380	                    if let Some((consecutive, last_error)) =
   381	                        self.record_claim_error(bead_id, &reason)
   382	                    {
   383	                        self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::ClaimErrorThreshold {
   384	                            bead_id: bead_id.clone(),
   385	                            consecutive_errors: consecutive,
   386	                            last_error: last_error.clone(),
   387	                        })?;
   388	                        // Set Error status on the bead.claim span
   389	                        tracing::Span::current().record("otel.status_code", 2u64);
   390	                        tracing::Span::current().record("otel.status_description", &last_error);
   391	                        return Ok(ClaimOutcome::Suspect {
   392	                            bead_id: bead_id.clone(),
   393	                            consecutive_errors: consecutive,
   394	                            last_error,
   395	                        });
   396	                    }
   397	                    // Set Error status on the bead.claim span
   398	                    tracing::Span::current().record("otel.status_code", 2u64);
   399	                    tracing::Span::current().record("otel.status_description", reason);
   400	                    return Ok(ClaimOutcome::StoreError(e));
   401	                }
   402	            }
   403	        }
   404	
   405	        // Exhausted all eligible candidates without success
   406	        tracing::Span::current().record("needle.claim.result", "all_race_lost");
   407	        // Set Error status on the bead.claim span
   408	        tracing::Span::current().record("otel.status_code", 2u64);
   409	        tracing::Span::current().record("otel.status_description", "all_race_lost");
   410	        Ok(ClaimOutcome::AllRaceLost)
   411	    }

   413	    /// Convenience: claim a single bead by ID (fetches the bead, then delegates
   414	    /// to `claim_next` with a single-element candidate list).
   415	    ///
   416	    /// The `exclusions` parameter allows the caller to pass beads that should
   417	    /// be skipped (e.g., beads that recently lost a claim race). This prevents
   418	    /// tight loops when multiple workers are racing on the same bead.

   420	    /// The `strand` parameter is optional; if not provided, defaults to "unknown".

   570	    let deadline = Instant::now() + FLOCK_TIMEOUT;
   571	    loop {
   572	        match file.try_lock_exclusive() {
   573	            Ok(()) => return Ok(file),
   574	            Err(ref e) if e.kind() == io::ErrorKind::WouldBlock => {
   575	                if Instant::now() >= deadline {
   576	                    return Err(anyhow!(
   577	                        "flock timeout after {}s on {}",
   578	                        FLOCK_TIMEOUT.as_secs(),
   579	                        lock_path.display()
   580	                    ));
   581	                }
   582	                tokio::time::sleep(FLOCK_POLL_INTERVAL).await;
   583	            }
   584	            Err(e) => return Err(e.into()),
   585	        }
   586	    }

  3393	    /// Force-flush all buffered events to disk (synchronous).
  3394	    ///
  3395	    /// Sends a flush request through the writer channel and waits (up to
  3396	    /// `timeout`) for the writer task to flush its BufWriter. Used after
  3397	    /// `worker.booting` so the event is visible on disk even if subsequent
  3398	    /// init steps block.
  3399	    ///
  3400	    /// NOTE: This uses `blocking_recv()` and must be called from outside a
  3401	    /// tokio runtime (e.g., in `run_worker` before `rt.block_on`). Use
  3402	    /// `force_flush_async()` from within async contexts.
  3403	    pub fn force_flush(&self, timeout: std::time::Duration) -> Result<()> {
  3404	        let (tx, rx) = tokio::sync::oneshot::channel();
  3405	        // Use try_lock() to avoid blocking indefinitely if the telemetry writer
  3406	        // is stuck holding the lock.
  3407	        match self.sender.try_lock() {
  3408	            Ok(guard) => {
  3409	                if let Some(ref s) = *guard {
  3410	                    s.send(WriterMessage::Flush(tx)).ok();
  3411	                }
  3412	            }
  3413	            Err(_) => {
  3414	                tracing::warn!("telemetry sender lock contended in force_flush, skipping flush");
  3415	                return Ok(()); // Don't fail — the writer will eventually flush
  3416	            }
  3417	        }
  3418	        // Block until the writer task flushes or timeout.
  3419	        // Spawn a thread to handle the blocking recv with a timeout.
  3420	        let handle = std::thread::spawn(move || rx.blocking_recv());
  3421	        let start = std::time::Instant::now();
  3422	        loop {
  3423	            if handle.is_finished() {
  3424	                return Ok(());
  3425	            }
  3426	            if start.elapsed() >= timeout {
  3427	                tracing::warn!("force_flush timed out after {:?}", timeout);
  3428	                return Ok(()); // Don't fail — the writer will eventually flush
  3429	            }
  3430	            std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(50));
  3431	        }
  3432	    }
  3433	
  3434	    /// Force-flush all buffered events to disk (async).
  3435	    ///
  3436	    /// Async version of `force_flush()` that can be called from within a
  3437	    /// tokio runtime. Use this in `Worker::run()` and other async contexts.
  3438	    pub async fn force_flush_async(&self, timeout: std::time::Duration) -> Result<()> {
  3439	        let (tx, rx) = tokio::sync::oneshot::channel();
  3440	        // Use try_lock() to avoid blocking indefinitely if the telemetry writer
  3441	        // is stuck holding the lock.
  3442	        match self.sender.try_lock() {
  3443	            Ok(guard) => {
  3444	                if let Some(ref s) = *guard {
  3445	                    s.send(WriterMessage::Flush(tx)).ok();
  3446	                }
  3447	            }
  3448	            Err(_) => {
  3449	                tracing::warn!(
  3450	                    "telemetry sender lock contended in force_flush_async, skipping flush"
  3451	                );
  3452	                return Ok(()); // Don't fail — the writer will eventually flush
  3453	            }
  3454	        }
  3455	        // Wait for the writer task to flush, with timeout.
  3456	        match tokio::time::timeout(timeout, rx).await {
  3457	            Ok(Ok(())) => Ok(()),
  3458	            Ok(Err(_)) => Ok(()), // Channel closed, writer already flushed
  3459	            Err(_) => {
  3460	                tracing::warn!("force_flush_async timed out after {:?}", timeout);
  3461	                Ok(())
  3462	            }
  3463	        }
  3464	    }

     1	//! Atomic bead claiming with per-workspace flock serialization.
     2	//!
     3	//! The Claimer wraps `BeadStore.claim()` with coordination that prevents
     4	//! thundering herd. A per-workspace flock serializes claim operations so
     5	//! workers take turns rather than racing on the same bead.
     6	//!
     7	//! Depends on: `types`, `bead_store`, `telemetry`.
     8	
     9	use std::collections::{HashMap, HashSet};
    10	use std::hash::{Hash, Hasher};

    12	use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

    21	use crate::types::{Bead, BeadId, BeadStatus, ClaimOutcome, ClaimResult};
    22	
    23	/// Flock timeout: maximum time to wait for the workspace lock.
    24	const FLOCK_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(10);
    25	
    26	/// Flock poll interval: time between lock acquisition attempts.
    27	const FLOCK_POLL_INTERVAL: Duration = Duration::from_millis(50);
    28	
    29	/// Number of consecutive claim errors before marking a bead suspect.
    30	const CLAIM_ERROR_THRESHOLD: u32 = 3;
    31	
    32	/// Maximum claim-related history entries allowed before a bead is quarantined.
    33	///
    34	/// A single claim can append more than one history entry (for example,
    35	/// `claimed` plus `assignee_changed`), so this is intentionally a hard safety
    36	/// budget rather than a claim-attempt count.  The backend is checked before
    37	/// each mutation whenever it exposes event history.
    38	const MAX_CLAIM_EVENTS_PER_BEAD: u32 = 100;
    39	
    40	/// Atomic bead claimer with workspace-level flock serialization.
    41	pub struct Claimer {
    42	    store: Arc<dyn BeadStore>,
    43	    lock_dir: PathBuf,
    44	    max_retries: u32,
    45	    retry_backoff_ms: u64,
    46	    telemetry: Telemetry,
    47	    /// Track consecutive claim errors per bead ID.
    48	    claim_errors: Arc<std::sync::Mutex<HashMap<BeadId, u32>>>,
    49	    /// Track total claim events emitted per bead ID for circuit-breaking.
    50	    claim_events: Arc<std::sync::Mutex<HashMap<BeadId, u32>>>,
    51	}
    52	
    53	impl Claimer {
    54	    /// Create a new Claimer.
    55	    ///
    56	    /// - `store`: bead store for verify + claim operations
    57	    /// - `lock_dir`: directory for flock files (default: `/tmp`)
    58	    /// - `max_retries`: maximum claim attempts before giving up (default: 5)
    59	    /// - `retry_backoff_ms`: base backoff between retries in ms (default: 100)
    60	    /// - `telemetry`: telemetry emitter
    61	    pub fn new(
    62	        store: Arc<dyn BeadStore>,
    63	        lock_dir: PathBuf,
    64	        max_retries: u32,
    65	        retry_backoff_ms: u64,
    66	        telemetry: Telemetry,
    67	    ) -> Self {
    68	        Claimer {
    69	            store,
    70	            lock_dir,
    71	            max_retries,
    72	            retry_backoff_ms,
    73	            telemetry,
    74	            claim_errors: Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(HashMap::new())),
    75	            claim_events: Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(HashMap::new())),
    76	        }
    77	    }
    78	
    79	    /// Record a claim error for a bead and check if the threshold is reached.
    80	    ///
    81	    /// Returns `Some((consecutive_errors, last_error))` if the bead has reached
    82	    /// the error threshold, `None` otherwise. This is distinct from race-lost:
    83	    /// claim errors are CLI/store failures, not contention.
    84	    fn record_claim_error(&self, bead_id: &BeadId, error: &str) -> Option<(u32, String)> {
    85	        let mut errors = self.claim_errors.lock().unwrap();
    86	        let count = errors.entry(bead_id.clone()).or_insert(0);
    87	        *count += 1;
    88	        let consecutive = *count;
    89	        let last_error = error.to_string();
    90	
    91	        if consecutive >= CLAIM_ERROR_THRESHOLD {
    92	            // Reset the counter after reaching threshold so subsequent attempts
    93	            // start fresh (avoids emitting the same error repeatedly)
    94	            errors.remove(bead_id);
    95	            Some((consecutive, last_error))
    96	        } else {
    97	            None
    98	        }
    99	    }
   100	
   101	    /// Clear claim errors for a bead (e.g., after a successful claim).
   102	    fn clear_claim_errors(&self, bead_id: &BeadId) {
   103	        let mut errors = self.claim_errors.lock().unwrap();
   104	        errors.remove(bead_id);
   105	    }

   107	    /// Check the in-memory fallback budget for backends that do not expose
   108	    /// claim history in their `show` projection.
   109	    ///
   110	    /// Returns `Some(total_events)` after the budget is exhausted.
   111	    fn check_event_limit(&self, bead_id: &BeadId) -> Option<u32> {
   112	        let mut events = self.claim_events.lock().unwrap();
   113	        let count = events.entry(bead_id.clone()).or_insert(0);

   144	    /// Attempt to claim the next available bead from the candidate list.
   145	    ///
   146	    /// Iterates candidates in priority order, skipping those in the exclusion
   147	    /// set. For each candidate, acquires a per-workspace flock, verifies the
   148	    /// bead is still claimable, and attempts the claim.
   149	    ///
   150	    /// The `strand` parameter is the name of the strand that initiated the claim
   151	    /// (e.g., "pluck", "mend"). This is emitted in telemetry for the
   152	    /// `needle.beads.claimed` metric's `strand` attribute.
   153	    ///
   154	    /// Returns:
   155	    /// - `Claimed(bead)`: successfully claimed a bead
   156	    /// - `AllRaceLost`: tried candidates, all race-lost
   157	    /// - `NoCandidates`: no candidates after filtering exclusions
   158	    /// - `StoreError(e)`: bead store or flock error
   159	    ///
   160	    /// NOTE: The caller is responsible for creating the `bead.claim` span
   161	    /// to ensure proper parent/child hierarchy (bead.claim should be a child
   162	    /// of bead.lifecycle, not strand.{name}).
   163	    pub async fn claim_next(
   164	        &self,
   165	        candidates: &[Bead],
   166	        actor: &str,
   167	        exclusions: &HashSet<BeadId>,
   168	        strand: &str,
   169	    ) -> Result<ClaimOutcome> {
   170	        let eligible: Vec<&Bead> = candidates
   171	            .iter()
   172	            .filter(|b| !exclusions.contains(&b.id))
   173	            .collect();
   174	
   175	        if eligible.is_empty() {
   176	            return Ok(ClaimOutcome::NoCandidates);
   177	        }
   178	
   179	        let mut attempts = 0u32;
   180	
   680	            {
   681	                let mut results = self.claim_results.lock().unwrap();
   682	                if !results.is_empty() {
   683	                    return Ok(results.remove(0));
   684	                }
   685	            }
   686	            // Default: claim succeeds
   687	            let mut bead = self
   688	                .beads
   689	                .lock()
   690	                .unwrap()
   691	                .iter()
   692	                .find(|b| b.id == *id)

   695	            bead.status = BeadStatus::InProgress;
   696	            bead.assignee = Some(actor.to_string());
   697	            Ok(ClaimResult::Claimed(bead))
   698	        }

  4100	impl Drop for Worker {
  4101	    fn drop(&mut self) {
  4102	        // Clear the global shutdown flag when the worker is dropped.
  4103	        // This prevents dangling pointers if the worker is dropped without
  4104	        // calling stop() (e.g., due to panic or early return).
  4105	        #[cfg(unix)]
  4106	        {
  4107	            clear_global_shutdown_flag();
  4108	        }
  4109	
  4110	        // Join the watchdog thread if it was started.
  4111	        // Set the trigger flag to signal the thread to exit.
  4112	        self.watchdog_triggered.store(true, Ordering::Release);
  4113	        if let Some(handle) = self.watchdog_handle.take() {
  4114	            // Don't block indefinitely joining the thread during drop.
  4115	            // If it doesn't exit within 1 second, we'll still continue.
  4116	            let _ = handle.join();
  4117	        }
  4118	    }
  4119	}

    39	/// Test helper for capturing and inspecting telemetry events.
    40	///
    41	/// Wraps a `Telemetry` emitter with a `MemorySink` to collect events
    42	/// during tests. Provides convenience methods for querying and asserting
    43	/// on captured events.
    44	///
    45	/// # Example
    46	///
    47	/// ```no_run
    48	/// use needle::telemetry::test_utils::TestHelper;
    49	///
    50	/// let helper = TestHelper::new("test-worker");
    51	///
    52	/// // Emit events through the helper's telemetry emitter
    53	/// helper.telemetry().emit(EventKind::WorkerStarted { ... }).unwrap();
    54	///
    55	/// // Query captured events
    56	/// let started_events = helper.events_by_type("worker.started");
    57	/// assert_eq!(started_events.len(), 1);
    58	///
    59	/// // Or use helper methods for assertions
    60	/// helper.assert_event_emitted("worker.started");
    61	/// helper.assert_event_count("worker.started", 1);
    62	/// ```
    63	#[cfg(any(test, feature = "integration"))]
    64	pub struct TestHelper {

    75	    /// Returns a helper that collects all emitted telemetry events in memory,
    76	    /// allowing tests to query and assert on them.
    77	    ///
    78	    /// # Arguments
    79	    ///
    80	    /// * `worker_id` - The worker ID to use for the telemetry emitter
    81	    ///
    82	    /// # Example
    83	    ///
    84	    /// ```no_run
    85	    /// let helper = TestHelper::new("test-worker");
    86	    /// ```
    87	    pub fn new(worker_id: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
    88	        let worker_id = worker_id.into();
    89	        let (sink, events) = MemorySink::new();
    90	        let telemetry = Telemetry::with_sink(worker_id, sink);
    91	        Self { telemetry, events }
    92	    }
    93	
    94	    /// Get a reference to the telemetry emitter for emitting events.
    95	    ///
    96	    /// # Example
    97	    ///
    98	    /// ```no_run
    99	    /// helper.telemetry().emit(EventKind::QueueEmpty).unwrap();
   100	    /// ```
   101	    pub fn telemetry(&self) -> &Telemetry {
   102	        &self.telemetry
   103	    }
   104	
   105	    /// Get all captured events as a vector.
   106	    ///
   107	    /// Returns a copy of all events collected so far. This acquires a lock
   108	    /// on the internal events vector, so it will block if another thread
   109	    /// is currently adding events.
   110	    pub fn all_events(&self) -> Vec<TelemetryEvent> {
   111	        self.events.lock().unwrap().clone()
   112	    }
   113	
   114	    /// Get events filtered by event type.
   115	    ///
   116	    /// Returns all events whose `event_type` matches the given pattern.
   117	    /// The pattern is an exact string match (not a glob pattern).
   118	    ///
   119	    /// # Arguments
   120	    ///
   121	    /// * `event_type` - The exact event type to filter by (e.g., "worker.started")
   122	    ///
   123	    /// # Example
   124	    ///
   125	    /// ```no_run
   126	    /// let started = helper.events_by_type("worker.started");
   127	    /// assert_eq!(started.len(), 1);
   128	    /// ```
   129	    pub fn events_by_type(&self, event_type: &str) -> Vec<TelemetryEvent> {
   130	        self.all_events()
   131	            .into_iter()
   132	            .filter(|e| e.event_type == event_type)
   133	            .collect()
   134	    }
   135	
   136	    /// Get events filtered by bead ID.
   137	    ///
   138	    /// Returns all events that have a `bead_id` field matching the given ID.
   139	    ///
   140	    /// # Arguments
   141	    ///
   142	    /// * `bead_id` - The bead ID to filter by
   143	    ///
   144	    /// # Example
   145	    ///
   146	    /// ```no_run
   147	    /// let bead_events = helper.events_by_bead_id("needle-abc123");
   148	    /// ```
   149	    pub fn events_by_bead_id(&self, bead_id: &str) -> Vec<TelemetryEvent> {
   150	        self.all_events()
   151	            .into_iter()
   152	            .filter(|e| {
   153	                e.bead_id
   154	                    .as_ref()
   155	                    .map(|b| b.as_ref() == bead_id)
   156	                    .unwrap_or(false)
   157	            })
   158	            .collect()
   159	    }

   177	        let events = self.events_by_type(event_type);
   178	        if events.is_empty() {
   179	            panic!(
   180	                "Expected event '{}' to be emitted, but no such events were captured",
  2920	    }

  2930	    /// Create a telemetry emitter that writes to a `FileSink`.
  2931	    ///
  2932	    /// Does not spawn any async tasks. Call [`start()`](Self::start) from
  2933	    /// within a tokio runtime context before emitting events.
  2934	    ///
  2935	    /// Writes `worker.booting` directly to the file before returning, so even
  2936	    /// if the writer thread fails to start, we have a trace in the JSONL log.
  2937	    pub fn new(worker_id: WorkerId) -> Self {
  2938	        let session_id = generate_session_id();
  2939	        let (sender, receiver) = mpsc::unbounded_channel();
  2940	
  2941	        let mut sinks: Vec<Box<dyn Sink>> = Vec::new();
  2942	        match FileSink::new(&worker_id, &session_id) {
  2943	            Ok(s) => {
  2944	                // Write boot event directly to file BEFORE spawning writer thread.
  2945	                // Uses a 5-second timeout to prevent indefinite blocking on hung filesystems.
  2946	                // This ensures we have a trace even if the writer thread fails to start.
  2947	                let version = env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION");
  2948	                if let Err(e) = s.write_boot_event_direct(&worker_id, &session_id, version) {
  2949	                    // Check if this is a timeout error (filesystem may be hung)
  2950	                    let error_msg = e.to_string();
  2951	                    if error_msg.contains("timed out")
  2952	                        || error_msg.contains("filesystem may be hung")
  2953	                    {
  2954	                        eprintln!(
  2955	                            "NEEDLE WARNING: boot event write timed out after 5s - filesystem may be hung or very slow"
  2956	                        );
  2957	                        eprintln!("  Continuing without boot event in log file. Worker will still function.");
  2958	                        eprintln!(
  2959	                            "  Check: disk space, NFS mounts, filesystem latency, I/O errors"
  2960	                        );
  2961	                    }
  2962	                    tracing::warn!(error = %e, "failed to write boot event directly to file");
  2963	                }
  2964	                sinks.push(Box::new(s));
  2965	            }
  2966	            Err(e) => tracing::warn!(error = %e, "failed to create telemetry file sink"),
  2967	        }
  2968	
  2969	        let sequence = Arc::new(AtomicU64::new(0));
  2970	        let pending = PendingWriter { receiver, sinks };
  2971	
  2972	        Telemetry {
  2973	            worker_id,
  2974	            session_id,
  2975	            sequence,
  2976	            sender: Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(Some(sender))),
  2977	            pending_writer: Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(Some(pending))),
  2978	            writer_handle: Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(None)),
  2979	            otlp_shutdown: Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(None)),
  2980	        }
  2981	    }

  3100	    /// Create a telemetry emitter from a `TelemetryConfig`.
  3101	    ///
  3102	    /// Selects the right constructor based on configured sinks:
  3103	    /// - OTLP enabled       → creates OTLP sink with async shutdown
  3104	    /// - Hooks configured   → [`with_hooks`](Self::with_hooks)
  3105	    /// - Stdout enabled     → [`with_stdout`](Self::with_stdout)
  3106	    /// - Otherwise          → [`new`](Self::new) (file sink only)
  3107	    pub fn from_config(worker_id: WorkerId, config: &TelemetryConfig) -> Result<Self> {
  3108	        Self::from_config_with_identity(worker_id, config, &TelemetryIdentity::default())
  3109	    }
  3110	
  3111	    /// Create a telemetry emitter from configuration with worker identity metadata.
  3112	    ///
  3113	    /// This is the construction path used by a running worker. Keeping the
  3114	    /// identity separate from `TelemetryConfig` avoids putting runtime-resolved
  3115	    /// adapter details into persisted configuration while ensuring every OTLP
  3116	    /// signal receives the same worker metadata.
  3117	    pub fn from_config_with_identity(
  3118	        worker_id: WorkerId,
  3119	        config: &TelemetryConfig,
  3120	        identity: &TelemetryIdentity,
  3121	    ) -> Result<Self> {
  3122	        let session_id = generate_session_id();
  3123	        let (sender, receiver) = mpsc::unbounded_channel();
  3124	
  3125	        let mut sinks: Vec<Box<dyn Sink>> = Vec::new();
  3126	        let mut otlp_shutdown = None;
  3127	        let mut file_sink: Option<Arc<FileSink>> = None;
  3128	
  3129	        // File sink is created only if enabled in config
  3130	        // When disabled, telemetry falls back to stdout/hook sinks only
  3131	        if config.file_sink.enabled {
  3132	            // Use configured log_dir if set, otherwise use default
  3133	            let file_sink_result = if let Some(ref log_dir) = config.file_sink.log_dir {
  3134	                FileSink::with_dir(log_dir.clone(), &worker_id, &session_id)
  3135	            } else {
  3136	                FileSink::new(&worker_id, &session_id)
  3137	            };
  3138	
  3139	            match file_sink_result {
  3140	                Ok(s) => {
  3141	                    // Write boot event directly to file BEFORE spawning writer thread.
  3142	                    // Uses a 5-second timeout to prevent indefinite blocking on hung filesystems.
  3143	                    let version = env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION");
  3144	                    if let Err(e) = s.write_boot_event_direct(&worker_id, &session_id, version) {
  3145	                        // Check if this is a timeout error (filesystem may be hung)
  3146	                        let error_msg = e.to_string();
  3147	                        if error_msg.contains("timed out")
  3148	                            || error_msg.contains("filesystem may be hung")
  3149	                        {
  3150	                            eprintln!(
  3151	                                "NEEDLE WARNING: boot event write timed out after 5s - filesystem may be hung or very slow"
  3152	                            );
  3153	                            eprintln!("  Continuing without boot event in log file. Worker will still function.");
  3154	                            eprintln!(
  3155	                                "  Check: disk space, NFS mounts, filesystem latency, I/O errors"
  3156	                            );
  3157	                        }
  3158	                        tracing::warn!(error = %e, "failed to write boot event directly to file");
  3159	                    }
  3160	                    file_sink = Some(Arc::new(s));
  3161	                    // Arc<FileSink> implements Sink via the blanket impl
  3162	                    if let Some(ref fs) = file_sink {
  3163	                        sinks.push(Box::new(Arc::clone(fs)));
  3164	                    }
  3165	                }
  3166	                Err(e) => tracing::warn!(error = %e, "failed to create telemetry file sink"),
  3167	            }
  3168	        }
  3169	
  3170	        // OTLP sink (feature-gated)
  3171	        #[cfg(feature = "otlp")]
  3172	        {
  3173	            if config.otlp_sink.enabled {
  3174	                // Convert Arc<FileSink> to Option<Box<dyn Sink>> for OtlpSink
  3175	                let file_sink_for_otlp = file_sink
  3176	                    .as_ref()
  3177	                    .map(|fs| Box::new(Arc::clone(fs)) as Box<dyn Sink>);
  3178	
  3179	                match OtlpSink::new(
  3180	                    worker_id.clone(),
  3181	                    session_id.clone(),
  3182	                    &config.otlp_sink,
  3183	                    file_sink_for_otlp,
  3184	                    identity.agent.as_deref(),
  3185	                    identity.model.as_deref(),
  3186	                    identity.workspace.as_deref().and_then(Path::to_str),
  3187	                ) {
  3188	                    Ok(otlp) => {
  3189	                        let otlp_arc = Arc::new(otlp);
  3190	                        sinks.push(Box::new(Arc::clone(&otlp_arc)));
  3191	                        otlp_shutdown = Some(OtlpShutdown::Sink(otlp_arc));
  3192	                        tracing::info!("OTLP sink initialized: {}", config.otlp_sink.endpoint);
  3193	                    }
  3194	                    Err(e) => {
  3195	                        tracing::warn!(error = %e, "failed to create OTLP sink, continuing without it");
  3196	                    }
  3197	                }
  3198	            }
  3199	        }
  3200	
  3201	        // Stdout sink
  3202	        if config.stdout_sink.enabled {
  3203	            sinks.push(Box::new(StdoutSink::new(&config.stdout_sink)));
  3204	        }
  3205	
  3206	        // Hook sinks
  3207	        if !config.hooks.is_empty() {
  3208	            sinks.push(Box::new(HookSink::new(&config.hooks)?));
  3209	        }
  3210	
  3211	        let sequence = Arc::new(AtomicU64::new(0));
  3212	        let pending = PendingWriter { receiver, sinks };
  3213	
  3214	        Ok(Telemetry {
  3215	            worker_id,
  3216	            session_id,
  3217	            sequence,
  3218	            sender: Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(Some(sender))),
  3219	            pending_writer: Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(Some(pending))),
  3220	            writer_handle: Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(None)),
  3221	            otlp_shutdown: Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(otlp_shutdown)),
  3222	        })
  3223	    }

   272	    async fn claim_auto_inner(&self, actor: &str) -> Result<ClaimResult> {
   273	        let values = HashMap::from([("actor", actor.to_string())]);
   274	        let stdout = self.run_operation("claim_auto", &values).await?;
   275	        let json: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(&stdout)

   279	            .or_else(|| json.pointer("/data/bead_id"))
   280	            .and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str)
   281	            .filter(|id| !id.is_empty());

   284	            None => Ok(ClaimResult::NotClaimable {
   285	                reason: "no beads available".to_string(),

   742	impl CliBeadStore {
   743	    async fn claim_via_batch(&self, id: &BeadId, actor: &str) -> Result<ClaimResult> {
   744	        let shown = self.show(id).await?;
   745	        if shown.status != BeadStatus::Open {
   746	            return Ok(ClaimResult::NotClaimable {
   747	                reason: format!("bead is {}, not open", shown.status),
   748	            });
   749	        }
   750	        if let Some(claimed_by) = shown.assignee {
   751	            return Ok(ClaimResult::RaceLost { claimed_by });
   752	        }
   753	
   754	        // bf 0.4.1 removed --assignee from `update`, but its transactional
   755	        // batch update operation still accepts status and assignee together.
   756	        self.run_bf_update_batch(id, Some("in_progress"), Some(actor))
   757	            .await
   758	            .with_context(|| format!("bf batch update {id} (claim) failed"))?;
   759	
   760	        let claimed = self.show(id).await?;
   761	        if claimed.assignee.as_deref() == Some(actor) {
   762	            Ok(ClaimResult::Claimed(claimed))
   763	        } else {
   764	            Ok(ClaimResult::RaceLost {
   765	                claimed_by: claimed.assignee.unwrap_or_else(|| "(unknown)".to_string()),
   766	            })
   767	        }
   768	    }

The existing OTLP sink already reduces `event.workspace` to a basename, and the earlier resource-propagation fix is present and closed. I’m going to make the workspace state shared by all cloned `Telemetry` handles, have all three emit paths read it, and update it at both successful claim paths. I’ll also cover the same-session repo switch and verify the OTLP attribute remains basename-only.

+    /// Update the workspace attached to subsequently emitted events.
+    ///
+    /// The path is kept internally so local sinks and query filters can retain
+    /// their existing behavior. The OTLP sink reduces it to a basename before
+    /// adding the browser-visible log attribute.
+    pub fn set_workspace(&self, workspace: impl Into<PathBuf>) {
+        let workspace = workspace.into();
+        match self.current_workspace.write() {
+            Ok(mut current) => *current = Some(workspace),
+            Err(poisoned) => {
+                tracing::warn!("telemetry workspace lock poisoned; recovering current workspace");
+                *poisoned.into_inner() = Some(workspace);
+            }
+        }
+    }
+
+    fn workspace_snapshot(&self) -> Option<PathBuf> {
+        match self.current_workspace.read() {
+            Ok(current) => current.clone(),
+            Err(poisoned) => {
+                tracing::warn!("telemetry workspace lock poisoned; recovering workspace snapshot");
+                poisoned.into_inner().clone()
+            }
+        }
+    }
+
+    fn make_event(&self, kind: &EventKind) -> TelemetryEvent {
+        let seq = self.sequence.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
+        let (trace_id, span_id) = current_trace_ids();
+        TelemetryEvent {
+            timestamp: Utc::now(),
+            event_type: kind.event_type().to_string(),
+            worker_id: self.worker_id.clone(),
+            session_id: self.session_id.clone(),
+            sequence: seq,
+            bead_id: kind.bead_id(),
+            workspace: self.workspace_snapshot(),
+            duration_ms: kind.duration_ms(),
+            data: kind.to_data(),
+            trace_id,
+            span_id,
+        }
+    }
+
     /// Emit an event. Non-blocking — returns immediately.
     ///
     /// Returns `Err` only if the channel is disconnected (background task died).

+    /// Update the workspace attached to subsequently emitted events.
+    ///
+    /// The path is kept internally so local sinks and query filters can retain
+    /// their existing behavior. The OTLP sink reduces it to a basename before
+    /// adding the browser-visible log attribute.
+    pub fn set_workspace(&self, workspace: impl Into<PathBuf>) {
+        let workspace = workspace.into();
+        match self.current_workspace.write() {
+            Ok(mut current) => *current = Some(workspace),
+            Err(poisoned) => {
+                tracing::warn!("telemetry workspace lock poisoned; recovering current workspace");
+                *poisoned.into_inner() = Some(workspace);
+            }
+        }
+    }
+
+    fn workspace_snapshot(&self) -> Option<PathBuf> {
+        match self.current_workspace.read() {
+            Ok(current) => current.clone(),
+            Err(poisoned) => {
+                tracing::warn!("telemetry workspace lock poisoned; recovering workspace snapshot");
+                poisoned.into_inner().clone()
+            }
+        }
+    }
+
+    fn make_event(&self, kind: &EventKind) -> TelemetryEvent {
+        let seq = self.sequence.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
+        let (trace_id, span_id) = current_trace_ids();
+        TelemetryEvent {
+            timestamp: Utc::now(),
+            event_type: kind.event_type().to_string(),
+            worker_id: self.worker_id.clone(),
+            session_id: self.session_id.clone(),
+            sequence: seq,
+            bead_id: kind.bead_id(),
+            workspace: self.workspace_snapshot(),
+            duration_ms: kind.duration_ms(),
+            data: kind.to_data(),
+            trace_id,
+            span_id,
+        }
+    }

     #[tokio::test]
+    async fn emitted_events_follow_workspace_changes_within_one_session() {
+        let (sink, events) = MemorySink::new();
+        let telemetry = Telemetry::with_sink("test-worker".to_string(), sink);
+
+        telemetry.set_workspace("/home/coding/commitgraph");
+        telemetry.emit(EventKind::QueueEmpty).unwrap();
+        telemetry.set_workspace("/home/coding/SEAM");
+        telemetry.emit_try_lock(EventKind::QueueEmpty).unwrap();
+
+        drop(telemetry);
+        tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(50)).await;
+
+        let collected = events.lock().unwrap();
+        assert_eq!(collected.len(), 2);
+        assert_eq!(
+            collected[0].workspace.as_deref(),
+            Some(std::path::Path::new("/home/coding/commitgraph"))
+        );
+        assert_eq!(
+            collected[1].workspace.as_deref(),
+            Some(std::path::Path::new("/home/coding/SEAM"))
+        );
+    }

+

The implementation is now in place: `Telemetry` owns a shared `RwLock` cell, `emit`, `emit_try_lock`, and `emit_sync` snapshot it through one constructor, and successful claims update it. Worker-side correction also handles backends that return `"."` for `source_repo`, so remote Explore claims do not overwrite the real workspace with a placeholder. +    /// The path is kept internally so local sinks and query filters can retain

+    pub fn set_workspace(&self, workspace: impl Into<PathBuf>) {
+        let workspace = workspace.into();
+        match self.current_workspace.write() {
+            Ok(mut current) => *current = Some(workspace),
+            Err(poisoned) => {
+                tracing::warn!("telemetry workspace lock poisoned; recovering current workspace");
+                *poisoned.into_inner() = Some(workspace);
+            }
+        }
+    }

+                tracing::warn!("telemetry workspace lock poisoned; recovering workspace snapshot");
+                poisoned.into_inner().clone()
+            }
+        }
+    }

  2873	/// Non-blocking telemetry emitter.
  2874	///
  2875	/// Cloning a `Telemetry` handle is cheap — it shares the same background
  2876	/// writer and sequence counter.
  2877	///
  2878	/// The writer task must be started by calling `start()` from within a tokio
  2879	/// runtime context. This is typically done at the beginning of `Worker::run()`.
  2880	#[derive(Clone)]
  2881	pub struct Telemetry {
  2882	    worker_id: WorkerId,
  2883	    session_id: String,
  2884	    sequence: Arc<AtomicU64>,
  2885	    /// Wrapped in Arc<Mutex<Option<...>>> so that `shutdown()` can drop the
  2886	    /// sender explicitly (closing the channel) even while clones still exist.
  2887	    sender: Arc<std::sync::Mutex<Option<mpsc::UnboundedSender<WriterMessage>>>>,
  2888	    /// Pending writer state that needs to be spawned in an async context.
  2889	    /// This is `Some` until `start()` is called.
  2890	    pending_writer: Arc<std::sync::Mutex<Option<PendingWriter>>>,
  2891	    /// JoinHandle for the background writer thread, set by `start()`.
  2892	    /// Uses std::thread::JoinHandle (not tokio::task::JoinHandle) because the
  2893	    /// writer runs in its own dedicated thread with its own tokio runtime,
  2894	    /// ensuring it can process messages before the main runtime's block_on().
  2895	    writer_handle: Arc<std::sync::Mutex<Option<std::thread::JoinHandle<()>>>>,
  2896	    /// OTLP sink shutdown handle (feature-gated).
  2897	    /// Stored separately so we can call its async shutdown method.
  2898	    otlp_shutdown: Arc<std::sync::Mutex<Option<OtlpShutdown>>>,
  2899	}

  3340	    /// Emit an event. Non-blocking — returns immediately.
  3470	    pub async fn force_flush_async(&self, timeout: std::time::Duration) -> Result<()> {
  3471	        let (tx, rx) = tokio::sync::oneshot::channel();
  3472	        // Use try_lock() to avoid blocking indefinitely if the telemetry writer
  3473	        // is stuck holding the lock.
  3474	        match self.sender.try_lock() {
  3475	            Ok(guard) => {
  3476	                if let Some(ref s) = *guard {
  3477	                    s.send(WriterMessage::Flush(tx)).ok();
  3478	                }
  3479	            }
  3480	            Err(_) => {
  3481	                tracing::warn!(
  3482	                    "telemetry sender lock contended in force_flush_async, skipping flush"
  3483	                );
  3484	                return Ok(()); // Don't fail — the writer will eventually flush
  3485	            }
  3486	        }
  3487	        // Wait for the writer task to flush, with timeout.
  3488	        match tokio::time::timeout(timeout, rx).await {
  3489	            Ok(Ok(())) => Ok(()),
  3490	            Ok(Err(_)) => Ok(()), // Channel closed, writer already flushed
  3491	            Err(_) => {
  3492	                tracing::warn!("force_flush_async timed out after {:?}", timeout);
  3493	                Ok(())
  3494	            }
  3495	        }
  3496	    }

  3503	    ///
  3504	    /// Returns `Err` if the pending writer is not available (already started)
  3505	    /// or if writing to the file fails.
  3506	    pub fn emit_sync(&self, kind: EventKind) -> Result<()> {
  3507	        let seq = self.sequence.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
  3508	        let (trace_id, span_id) = current_trace_ids();

  3510	            timestamp: Utc::now(),

  3517	            duration_ms: kind.duration_ms(),
  3518	            data: kind.to_data(),
  3519	            trace_id,
  3520	            span_id,
  3521	        };
  3522	
  3523	        // Take the pending writer temporarily to write directly to sinks.
  3524	        let pending_guard = self.pending_writer.lock().unwrap();

  3526	            // Write directly to each sink (typically just FileSink).
  3527	            for sink in &pending.sinks {
  3528	                if let Err(e) = sink.accept(&event) {
  3529	                    tracing::warn!(error = %e, "sync emit to sink failed");
  3530	                }
  3531	            }
  3532	            Ok(())

  3535	            Err(anyhow::anyhow!("cannot emit_sync after start()"))

+    pub fn set_workspace(&self, workspace: impl Into<PathBuf>) {

+        match self.current_workspace.write() {
+            Ok(mut current) => *current = Some(workspace),
+            Err(poisoned) => {

+    /// Update the workspace attached to subsequently emitted events.
+    ///
+    /// The path is kept internally so local sinks and query filters can retain
+    /// their existing behavior. The OTLP sink reduces it to a basename before
+    /// adding the browser-visible log attribute.
+    pub fn set_workspace(&self, workspace: impl Into<PathBuf>) {
+        let workspace = workspace.into();
+        match self.current_workspace.write() {
+            Ok(mut current) => *current = Some(workspace),
+            Err(poisoned) => {
+                tracing::warn!("telemetry workspace lock poisoned; recovering current workspace");
+                *poisoned.into_inner() = Some(workspace);
+            }
+        }
+    }
+
+    fn workspace_snapshot(&self) -> Option<PathBuf> {
+        match self.current_workspace.read() {
+            Ok(current) => current.clone(),
+            Err(poisoned) => {
+                tracing::warn!("telemetry workspace lock poisoned; recovering workspace snapshot");
+                poisoned.into_inner().clone()
+            }
+        }
+    }
+
+    fn make_event(&self, kind: &EventKind) -> TelemetryEvent {
+        let seq = self.sequence.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
+        let (trace_id, span_id) = current_trace_ids();
+        TelemetryEvent {
+            timestamp: Utc::now(),
+            event_type: kind.event_type().to_string(),
+            worker_id: self.worker_id.clone(),
+            session_id: self.session_id.clone(),
+            sequence: seq,
+            bead_id: kind.bead_id(),
+            workspace: self.workspace_snapshot(),
+            duration_ms: kind.duration_ms(),
+            data: kind.to_data(),
+            trace_id,
+            span_id,
+        }
+    }

+        let second = make_bead("needle-workspace-second", "/tmp/needle-workspace-second");
+        let store = Arc::new(MockBeadStore::new(vec![first.clone(), second.clone()]));
+        let (sink, events) = MemorySink::new();

+        let claimer = Claimer::new(store, std::env::temp_dir(), 5, 10, telemetry.clone());
+
+        claimer
+            .claim_next(
+                std::slice::from_ref(&first),
+                "worker-1",
+                &HashSet::new(),
+                "test-strand",
+            )
+            .await
+            .unwrap();
+        claimer
+            .claim_next(
+                std::slice::from_ref(&second),
+                "worker-1",
+                &HashSet::new(),
+                "test-strand",
+            )
+            .await
+            .unwrap();
+
+        drop(claimer);
+        drop(telemetry);
+        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50)).await;
+
+        let successes: Vec<_> = events
+            .lock()
+            .unwrap()
+            .iter()
+            .filter(|event| event.event_type == "bead.claim.succeeded")
+            .cloned()
+            .collect();
+        assert_eq!(successes.len(), 2);
+        assert_eq!(
+            successes[0].workspace.as_deref(),
+            Some(first.workspace.as_path())
+        );
+        assert_eq!(
+            successes[1].workspace.as_deref(),
+            Some(second.workspace.as_path())
+        );
+    }

+    /// The path is kept internally so local sinks and query filters can retain
+    /// their existing behavior. The OTLP sink reduces it to a basename before
+    /// adding the browser-visible log attribute.
+    pub fn set_workspace(&self, workspace: impl Into<PathBuf>) {
+        let workspace = workspace.into();
+        match self.current_workspace.write() {
+            Ok(mut current) => *current = Some(workspace),
+            Err(poisoned) => {
+                tracing::warn!("telemetry workspace lock poisoned; recovering current workspace");
+                *poisoned.into_inner() = Some(workspace);
+            }
+        }
+    }

+            Err(poisoned) => {
+                tracing::warn!("telemetry workspace lock poisoned; recovering workspace snapshot");
+                poisoned.into_inner().clone()
+            }
+        }
+    }

+    pub fn set_workspace(&self, workspace: impl Into<PathBuf>) {
+        let workspace = workspace.into();
+        match self.current_workspace.write() {
+            Ok(mut current) => *current = Some(workspace),
+            Err(poisoned) => {
+                tracing::warn!("telemetry workspace lock poisoned; recovering current workspace");
+                *poisoned.into_inner() = Some(workspace);
+            }
+        }
+    }

+                poisoned.into_inner().clone()

+    pub fn set_workspace(&self, workspace: impl Into<PathBuf>) {

+        match self.current_workspace.write() {

//! Shipped-work verification: did a bead's closure correspond to real,
//! durable output?
//!
//! Gated by `worker.enforce_shipped_work` (default `true`). Runs only when an
//! agent has already closed the bead (see `outcome::handle_success`). Passes
//! if either:
//! - a commit was made since dispatch started (per the `validation::predispatch`
//!   snapshot) that touches at least one file outside `notes/`/`.beads/`, and
//!   that commit has been pushed to the upstream remote; or
//! - the bead's own `notes` field changed during this dispatch — i.e. the agent
//!   recorded a bead note explaining why no code change was needed.
//!
//! With no snapshot the gate has no baseline and **fails open** — it cannot tell
//! a commit made during the dispatch from one that predates it, and releasing on
//! "don't know" would recreate the retry loop it exists to stop.
//!
//! Deliberately does NOT accept a commit touching only `notes/`/`.beads/` as
//! sufficient on its own: a prior incident (see docs/notes on ARMOR's
//! commit-storm) showed a worker stuck retrying an uncompletable bead will
//! happily satisfy a bare "must have a commit" rule by committing a trivial
//! "still blocked" doc file every cycle, each one triggering paired CI
//! version-bump commits. Recording that kind of status belongs on the bead
//! through the workspace's configured backend, not in git history.
//!
//! # Why not `updated_at`
//!
//! The original fallback compared `post.updated_at > pre.updated_at`. That is
//! unsound: `bf close` *is* an update, so the timestamp always advances on the
//! exact path the gate exists to judge — an agent that closed a bead having
//! shipped nothing. Combined with a missing snapshot writer, this made the gate
//! inert from the day it shipped (2026-07-30) until this change: no closure was
//! ever rejected, and no bead ever received the `verification-failed` label.
//! Comparing the `notes` field instead keys on a deliberate note update.
//!
//! Depends on: `types`, `validation::predispatch`.

66:    store: &Arc<dyn BeadStore>,

+    pub fn set_workspace(&self, workspace: impl Into<PathBuf>) {
+        let workspace = workspace.into();
+        match self.current_workspace.write() {
+            Ok(mut current) => *current = Some(workspace),
+            Err(poisoned) => {
+                tracing::warn!("telemetry workspace lock poisoned; recovering current workspace");
+                *poisoned.into_inner() = Some(workspace);
+            }
+        }
+    }

+                poisoned.into_inner().clone()

+        }

+                &HashSet::new(),
+                "test-strand",

+        drop(telemetry);

+    pub fn set_workspace(&self, workspace: impl Into<PathBuf>) {
+        let workspace = workspace.into();
+        match self.current_workspace.write() {
+            Ok(mut current) => *current = Some(workspace),
+            Err(poisoned) => {
+                tracing::warn!("telemetry workspace lock poisoned; recovering current workspace");
+                *poisoned.into_inner() = Some(workspace);
+            }
+        }
+    }

+    pub fn set_workspace(&self, workspace: impl Into<PathBuf>) {
+        let workspace = workspace.into();
+        match self.current_workspace.write() {
+            Ok(mut current) => *current = Some(workspace),
+            Err(poisoned) => {
+                tracing::warn!("telemetry workspace lock poisoned; recovering current workspace");
+                *poisoned.into_inner() = Some(workspace);

+        }
